name: Automic Vault
description: Automic Vault detects secret exposure, hardens packages that work with secrets, encrypts .env files, and monitors the tools you install with Homebrew, npm, pip, and curl one-liners.
short_description: Don't let your own tools own you.
full_description: From the creator of Homebrew, Automic Vault finds tokens, credentials, and helper leaks while they are still on your machine, moves plaintext credentials off disk and into Keychain, installs tools immutably, provides dotenvx-compatible .env encryption, and monitors Homebrew, npm, pip, and curl workflows for new hazards.
positioning: Don't let your own tools own you

sections.title: Supply chain attacks are up. Your credentials are the prize.
sections.subtitle: Automic Vault finds tokens, credentials, and helper leaks while they're still on your machine.

sections.title: Agents can run your tools without rewriting them.
sections.subtitle: Sealed installs. Controlled updates. Nothing changes without you.

sections.title: Encrypt .env. Break nothing.

sections.subtitle: Homebrew, npm, pip, curl: keep using all of it. We'll flag risky changes.

sections.title: Homebrew made installing tools normal. Automic Vault adds the local boundary.
Free, open source local security for agent toolchains.

exposure_examples.summary: Prints a GitHub bearer token that an agent, script, or compromised tool can copy into API calls.
Turns a readable dotfile into cloud account access.
Asks the local credential helper to reveal repository credentials, even when there is no obvious token file.

founder_context: Homebrew made installing tools normal. Automic Vault adds the local boundary. Max Howell created Homebrew, and Automic Vault applies that package-management background to local package roots, command stubs, secret helpers, and monitoring boundaries for AI agents on macOS.

security_methods_and_gaps.title: Automic Vault Security Methods and Gaps
security_methods_and_gaps.description: A candid white paper on Automic Vault controls, caveats, holes, successes, and hardening work.

use_cases: Surface tokens, credentials, and helper leaks while they are still on the developer's machine.
Move plaintext credentials off disk and into Keychain, out of reach of agents and malware.

Expose credentials through native helper protocols such as AWS credential_process, Kubernetes ExecCredential, Cargo credential providers, Docker-compatible registry helpers, and WakaTime api_key_vault_cmd.
Install packages immutably so agents can run tools but cannot rewrite them.
Encrypt dotenvx-compatible .env files while keeping keys in Keychain and preserving the existing workflow.
Monitor Homebrew, npm, pip, and curl workflows and flag when something is wrong.
